glossary.definition: The role responsible for decisions and records in the defined workflow.
A point where a record moves from one person or system to another.
Testable statements used to judge software against the team's workflow.
The coverage defined for an audit program or an individual audit, including the processes covered and, as relevant, sites, shifts and period.
The requirements and internal procedures used as references for an audit.
What an auditor saw, read or was told, recorded in enough detail for someone else to check it.
Questions about how a process works, including who starts it, what record it creates, who checks it and what happens when something goes wrong.
A judgment drawn from observations and measured against criteria.
The evidence, checker and timing specified for following up a finding.
A check of whether an action worked, which may need to occur after the action is carried out.
The point at which the new system becomes the working record.
An inventory class for records needed for planning or follow-up.
An inventory class for records worth keeping and making searchable but not used in daily work.
An inventory class for records kept in their existing location with a pointer from the new system.
An inventory class for records no longer needed, subject to retention rules.
A test of whether representative users can perform work in the system with their records and constraints.
Bringing groups of users or parts of the audit program into the system in a planned order.

example.label: Illustrative example
example.description: An unnamed Canadian manufacturer evaluates internal audit management software for one production workflow; all situations and records are hypothetical, not customer results.

reviewedChapters.summary: The page follows the assigned workflow-mapping brief, uses supported claims and nearby citations, and labels its examples as hypothetical. No FAQ is assigned or included.
decisions: Which workflow break to solve first and whether to accept the problem statement
How to dispose of missing or disputed records
Which records are authoritative and whether to accept the record map

Which roles own handoffs and decisions, including backup ownership
How to handle unfilled roles, conflicts of interest and unreachable owners
Which acceptance criteria are must-haves, should-haves or could-haves and what constitutes a pass
How to handle criteria that cannot be tested or conflict

decisions: Which candidates proceed to demonstration
Whether to request a trial or drop a candidate with a must-have not shown
Whether each demonstration scenario passed, failed or was not shown

Whether evidence and permission tests meet the team's criteria

Which product to recommend and whether top management accepts the recommendation
How to handle an incomplete quote

reviewedChapters.title: Planning the internal audit program: Internal audit management software
reviewedChapters.summary: The page covers the assigned planning decisions with supported citations, actionable evaluation questions and labeled hypothetical examples. No FAQ is assigned or included.
decisions: Define and accept program and individual audit scopes, including exclusions and their reasons.
Resolve disputed or insufficiently described scope, escalating unresolved cases.
Assign auditors based on competence and impartiality.
Decide whether to apply an added control, delay an audit or seek outside help when no impartial auditor is available.
Accept audit dates and sampled activities based on priorities, relevant cycles and shifts, and reduced-frequency justifications.
Reschedule or change sampling when an area is unavailable.
Approve or reject moving, adding or canceling an audit based on the reason and effect on coverage.
Decide how to handle short-notice change requests or requests from outside the quality function.

reviewedChapters.title: Collecting and connecting audit evidence: Internal audit management software
reviewedChapters.summary: The page covers the assigned evidence-collection workflows with supported citations, actionable demonstration tests and labeled hypothetical examples. No FAQ was assigned or included.
decisions: Whether to accept or return the checklist and how to resolve unsuitable or disputed questions.
Whether the observation-recording method is acceptable and how to capture observations without a connection or device.
Whether each evidence-to-criterion link is sound and how to handle evidence without a matching criterion or a criterion without evidence.
Which user types may see or change each record type and whether the access configuration passes the approved rules.
Whether to grant, narrow or refuse temporary access and how to handle an access rule the product cannot enforce.

reviewedChapters.title: Recording and reviewing findings: Internal audit management software
reviewedChapters.summary: The page follows the assigned workflow brief, uses the supplied source claims appropriately, and labels its examples as hypothetical. No FAQ is assigned or included.
decisions: Whether an observation becomes a finding and which category applies.
Whether to request more evidence, hold or escalate an observation that does not fit a category.
Whether supporting evidence is relevant, sufficient and retrievable, or the finding should be returned.
Whether to collect more evidence, hold or withdraw a finding when evidence is inaccessible or disputed.
Who owns the response and by when, including reassignment or escalation when ownership is not accepted.
Whether a disputed finding stands, is revised, is withdrawn or is held for more evidence.
Who independently reviews and accepts a dispute decision when the quality manager is involved.

Accept or reject implementation evidence and decide whether closure must wait for an effectiveness check.
Approve and record an alternative control when an independent checker is unavailable.
Reopen or decline reopening a finding, including deciding ownership and timing.
Delegate a reopening decision when the quality manager or original checker is involved in a dispute.
Accept or hold a program report, resolve untraceable figures or missing coverage, and decide what actions follow.

Whether to pause, roll back or continue with a workaround when a serious problem occurs.
Whether to accept rollout as complete or request further action.
Whether retraining, reconfiguration or vendor help is needed for low adoption or increased workload.

reviewedChapters.title: Maintaining the system and choosing next steps: Internal audit management software
